WORKSHEET · CLASS 26 · AGES 4 YEARS

Magic Flower Color Garden Worksheet for Age 4

Age 4 YearsClass 26 · ColorsType Printable PDFPlays with <a href="/preschool/colors/adventures/magic-flower-color-garden/">the online game</a>

A flower with empty petals: color them one by one and count your colors at the end.

On the sheet: Color every petal — then count how many different colors you used.

THE ACTUAL WORKSHEET

Exactly what you’ll print.

This is the real sheet — the same file the buttons above hand you. Title, instructions, the activity itself, and a grown-up answer line where it helps.

Download Free Worksheet ↓ Play This Activity Online ↗

The PDF is a real printable file (A4, prints fine on US Letter). The print button prints only the worksheet — never the website around it. No sign-up, nothing stored.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Petal-by-petal coloring is the garden game’s pace, and it suits paper perfectly: each petal is one small decision, one color name, one careful fill. The final count turns the whole sheet into a color survey.

  • Petal-by-petal coloring
  • Color naming each time
  • Counting the colors used
  • Staying inside petal curves
HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Set up a little paint corner

    Crayons, pencils or paints all work. Put the color key where your child can see it and let them pick where to start.

  2. Name colors as they appear

    “You made the wing green!” Naming in the moment builds the color words faster than any flashcard.

  3. Ask about choices, not correctness

    “Tell me about this part” beats “is that the right color?” Creative choices are never graded here.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Black-and-white printing is a feature

The sheets print happily in grayscale — your child invents the colors, which is even better practice.

Mix on paper too

For the mixing sheets, keep a jar of water and let your child test each recipe with real paint afterwards.

Display the finished art

The fridge gallery matters. A child whose work is shown keeps making work.

Answer guide

Count the DISTINCT colors your child used (petals can share). More than five different colors is flower-garden gold.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class and the game behind it.

Play the game on screen first, print the worksheet second — or the other way round; they practice the same skill in two languages.
